AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 5, 2020
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE
PROVISIONS OF THE GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-25-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC AND TELECONFERENCED. TO PARTICIPATE IN A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN
EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR CALL (562) 929-5720 BEFORE 5 P.M. ON MEETING DAY
TO REQUEST A CALL DURING THE MEETING FOR A SPECIFIC ITEM OR ORAL COMMUNICATIONS.
DETAILS ARE AVAILABLE ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393, which is also where the meeting may be viewed.
  6:15 PM
  VIA TELECONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNCIL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957: THREAT
  TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County
  Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: APN 8056-017-901; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the
  City and Penny Reeves, Norwalk Auto Auction; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Councilmember Valencia

FLAG SALUTE
  Councilmember Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS None scheduled.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS
  COVID-10 Update.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of April 18,
  21, 23, 27, and 28 2020. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period March 22, 2020 – April 4,
  2020, in the total amount of $944,787.13. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April
  16 – April 28, 2020, in the total amount of $3,349,528.41. 640
   Report

  4.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – APRIL 22, 2020 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Synopsis

  5.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-27 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – AGREEMENT AMENDMENT - SENIOR
  NUTRITION PROGRAM VEHICLE PROCUREMENT - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-27, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS AND APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO THE
  AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AGING
  COMMUNITY SERVICES FOR ELDERLY NUTRITION PROGRAM SERVICES FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2019/20 TO PURCHASE TWO VEHICLES FOR MEAL DELIVERY, in the amount of
  $105,880; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 2, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney. 425-02-03

  Report

  6.  APPROVAL OF TRACT MAP NO. 82678, A LIVE-WORK CONDOMINIUM SUBDIVISION LOCATED
  AT 13211 SAN ANTONIO DRIVE, ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 20-08 – Staff recommends City Council
  approve Tract Map No. 82678 conditioned on the execution of the improvement guarantee required by
  Norwalk Municipal Code Section 16.03.160. 320-06-82678

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 – SUBRECIPIENT AGREEMENT FOR THE USE OF
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT FUNDS - Staff recommends City Council approve
  Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with Jovenes, Inc., to reallocate funding in an amount not to
  exceed $65,433 to administer the Norwalk Safe House for Youth Program; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute Amendment No. 1, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  8.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

  9.  FISCAL AD HOC COMMITTEE - Staff seeks City Council direction.

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 20-28 – APPROVING THE COMMUNITY DVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND
  HOME 2020-2025 CONSOLIDATED PLAN, FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, AND
  ANALYSIS OF IMPEDIMENTS TO FAIR HOUSING CHOICE AND AN APPLICATION FOR CDBG AND
  HOME FUNDING FOR FY2020/2021 - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-28, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME 2020-
  2025 CONSOLIDATED PLAN, FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, AND ANALYSIS
  OF IMPEDIMENTS TO FAIR HOUSING CHOICE AND AN APPLICATION FOR CDBG AND
  HOME FUNDING FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO
  EXECUTE AND TRANSMIT ALL REQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO THE UNITED STATES
   DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute and transmit all required documents to the United States
  Department of Housing and Urban Development.

  Report

  Attachment

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 20-30 - APPROVING PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2029 AND
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-31 APPROVING DENSITY BONUS AGREEMENT FOR 14815 PIONEER
  BOULEVARD - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-30, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2029; and

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 20-31, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING A DENSITY BONUS AGREEMENT WITH FLORENCE HOMES, LLC
  FOR 14815 PIONEER BOULEVARD.
  RESOLUTIONS

  Report

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 20-29 - REQUESTING SUPPORT FOR THE LOS ANGELES REGIONAL WATER
  QUALITY CONTROL BOARD TO REDUCE MUNICIPAL SEPARATE STORM SEWER SYSTEM
  PERMIT REQUIREMENTS FOR LOS ANGELES COUNTY – Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 20-29 – A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  REQUESTING THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA AND STATE LEGISLATIVE
  ELECTEDS URGE THE LOS ANGELES REGIONAL WATER QUALITY CONTROL BOARD TO
  REDUCE MUNICIPAL SEPARATE STORM SEWER SYSTEM PERMIT REQUIREMENTS FOR LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY.

  Report

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 20-32 – FISCAL YEAR 20219/10 COVID-19 FINANCIAL IMPACT BUDGET
  AMENDMENT – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-32, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING AMENDMENTS TO THE FISCAL YEAR
  2019/20 BUDGET DUE TO THE COVID-19 NEGATIVE FINANCIAL IMPACT.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated April 30, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
